articles.author: Jasmine Garsd
articles.description: A new study shows the steep economic cost of 2025's ICE raids in Chicago. Fear kept many immigrants home, draining the area of more than $1.26 billion in lost retail, restaurant, and sales-tax revenue.
articles.title: New report shows the economic toll of ICE raids

articles.author: Michael Kaloki
articles.description: Kenya's president orders a crackdown on foreigners running small businesses, amid accusations of xenophobia.
articles.title: Kenya's foreign trader crackdown sparks fear among migrant communities

articles.author: Andrew Limbong
articles.description: Bunch has spent the last few months defending the Smithsonian against attacks from President Trump. In a statement, Bunch says he leaves with "mixed emotions."
articles.title: Smithsonian chief Lonnie G. Bunch III resigns

articles.author: Raina Douris
articles.description: Caroline Rose's new album, Gentling the Horse at the Walt Whitman Mall, is out Oct. 23.
articles.title: How Caroline Rose threw out the rulebook on their latest album

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: A government statement said on Tuesday social media platforms would be required to send a notification to new and existing users offering them a choice over their default feed.
articles.title: Australian social media users to be offered choice to opt out of algorithms

articles.author: Lauren Frayer
articles.description: France, Canada and other countries joined the U.K. in banning goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Israel said it would close the British Consulate among other measures.
articles.title: U.K. accuses Israeli settlers of 'ethnic cleansing' in West Bank and bans their goods

articles.author: Ruchi Kumar
articles.description: In 2024, the ruling Taliban pledged to use flogging as well as stoning to punish people for not following certain of their precepts — committing adultery, running secret schools for girls. Have they followed through?
articles.title: Whatever happened to the Taliban threat: 'We will flog the women'?

articles.author: Steve Inskeep
articles.description: Chrystia Freeland understands the U.S.-Canada relationship from her time at the negotiating table. Here's what she sees now.
articles.title: Chrystia Freeland negotiated with Trump. Now she's watching a trade war unfold

articles.author: Paddy Hirsch
articles.description: A K means the rich and poor are pulling apart. A C supposedly means they're coming back together. We hear the case for both. Which letter you see may depend on what you choose to pay attention to.
articles.title: Has the economy gone C-shaped?

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The attacks come after weeks of escalating clashes between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen, which shattered a four-year truce in the country's civil war.
articles.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia ignite fires at oil facilities and wound 73 people

articles.author: Kat Lay, Global health correspondent
articles.description:
Key regions of the brain linked to movement, learning and emotions were affected and may lead to cognitive problems 
Babies born to mothers with anaemia have smaller brains, particularly in key regions linked to movement, learning and the regulation of emotion, according to a study.
Researchers said the differences, first detected at the age of one, could lead to cognitive problems when children started school.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Babies born to anaemic mothers have smaller brains, study finds

articles.author: Krishani Dhanji
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live
Albanese dismisses concerns over powers in digital duty of care bill
Anthony Albanese says the Nationals leader, Matt Canavan, is being “disingenuous” over his criticisms that the communications minister, Anika Wells, will have too much power under the new digital duty of care legislation.
The eSafety commissioner will of course provide the advice, but Matt Canavan actually knows that he’s being disingenuous because all of these things will be disallowable. That is, will be up to the whole parliament, like the other previous laws have been.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Politics live: Trump administration warns Australia after social media algorithm reform; Albanese mourns ‘true one-off’ in d’Alpuget

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
More than 1,000 flights cancelled with disruption continuing on Wednesday and airlines calling for overhaul after third incident in just over three years

UK airport disruption: what are your rights?

Flight delays and cancellations were expected to continue into Wednesday at UK airports after another air traffic control failure kept planes grounded for hours, affecting hundreds of thousands of passengers.
At least 177 flights scheduled for Wednesday to and from UK airports had been cancelled, plane tracking site Flightradar24 said, “nearly all at London Heathrow”. More than 1,000 were cancelled by about 8pm on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK air traffic control breakdown strands hundreds of thousands of passengers

articles.author: Penry Buckley
articles.description:
Jeremy Greenwood tells inquiry note contained agreement with Jean Nassif as counsel assisting says ‘threads of your story pull apart very quickly’
A Liberal operative has denied making up a “pink” or “fuchsia”-coloured piece of paper which he says was the record of an agreement with a property developer worth up to $5m, a corruption inquiry has heard.
Jeremy Greenwood told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Wednesday that the note, which he did not mention in a preliminary interview with the watchdog, was not a “recent invention”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Liberal operative denies he invented pink paper record of agreement with fugitive developer, Icac hears

articles.author: Dani Anguiano, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Missouri congressional maps thrown into chaos after conflicting court rulings

Sign up for US Breaking News emails

Further down the ballot in New Hampshire, the Democratic primary for Chris Pappas’s House seat has drawn eight candidates, with Stefany Shaheen – daughter of the outgoing senator – and Maura Sullivan, a former Obama administration official, leading the field.
The district, long purple, has been reliably blue since 2017. Republicans now see it as flippable, and Donald Trump has endorsed Anthony DiLorenzo, a businessman who owns several car dealerships, in the GOP race.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US supreme court rejects Missouri Republicans’ appeal to use Trump-backed congressional map in midterms – as it happened

articles.author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
articles.description:
The five people killed were employees of an aircraft cleaning company who were in a van struck by the plane after it overran the Miami airport runway

At least five dead after Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport

Officials in Florida on Tuesday said evidence collected from Saturday’s Amazon cargo plane crash at Miami international airport suggests the pilots considered aborting the flight’s landing before it crashed and killed five people on the ground.
At a press conference Tuesday evening, officials from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) released data from the plane’s “black box” flight data recorder, which was recovered from the wreckage on Monday, indicating pilots initiated a “go-around”, or aborted landing, seconds before impact.
Reuters contributed reporting
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pilots tried to abort landing seconds before deadly Amazon cargo plane crash that killed five

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
Roni Carlson, in wake of mistrial, says holdout juror could not be persuaded while colleague calls him ‘very arrogant’
A lone juror in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of the murder of her three children, would not agree to acquit Clancy despite expressing reasonable doubt about whether she was guilty, the jury’s foreperson said in an interview airing Monday.
Speaking to NBC 10 Boston just days after Clancy’s trial ended in a mistrial, Roni Carlson, the foreperson, confirmed there was one holdout juror who would not be persuaded to acquit Clancy due to insanity.
In the US, call the national maternal health hotline on 1-833-852-6262. In the UK, the Pandas foundation offers support via WhatsApp on 07903 508334. In Australia, the national maternal and perinatal mental health hotline is 1300 726 306.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lindsay Clancy juror had reasonable doubt but would not agree to acquit, foreperson says

articles.author: Tom McIlroy and Ben Doherty
articles.description:
Penny Wong has concerns about blanket ban announced by UK, France and Canada, but says new ‘targeted measures’ planned over Israeli settlers

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia is preparing another round of sanctions against Israel but has stopped short of joining the UK in banning trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
Overnight, the UK government offered its strongest condemnation yet of Israel’s occupation, with the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, calling efforts to control the West Bank unlawful. He said his government agreed there was “ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in areas of the West Bank, perpetrated by settler terrorists”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia considers new Israel sanctions but won’t join UK in banning trade with ‘settler terrorists’

articles.author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
articles.description:
Exclusive: The Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission, which has access to NDIA data, used Palantir as part of a multi-agency fraud taskforce

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Personal information of national disability insurance scheme participants may have ended up in controversial software company Palantir’s analytics platform as part of a massive multi-agency sharing program investigating fraud, Guardian Australia can reveal.
There have been calls to ban the use of Palantir’s software by the Australian government since May, after it implied some cultures are inferior to others in a manifesto described by one UK MP as the “ramblings of a supervillain”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NDIS data may have ended up in Palantir’s analytics platform as part of efforts to curb fraud

articles.author: Shrai Popat in Washington
articles.description:
Tit-for-tat violence surges again in region, with tankers struck by the US in the Gulf of Oman, and reprisal attacks by Iran on a US base in Jordan
The US military on Tuesday said it “destroyed” multiple Iranian tankers, after Iran attempted to strike a US navy warship with ballistic missiles, as violence once again surged across the region, pushing the price of oil close to $100 a barrel.
American forces struck the tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Iran’s Kharg Island, US central command (Centcom) said in a statement, adding that American forces “directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US says Iranian tankers ‘destroyed’ after missile attacks on American warship

articles.author: Victoria Bekiempis
articles.description:
Documents available through an online portal launched three days before the 25th anniversary of September 11
New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration has released more than 170,000 pages of municipal records involving the impact of the September 11 attacks on air quality health, as well as the city’s response.
Mamdani announced the documents and an online portal for accessing them on Tuesday. The release comes alongside the settlement of two lawsuits pursued by 9/11 Health Watch, which fought for access to these long-withheld documents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mamdani releases 170,000 pages of records regarding impact on air quality of 9/11 attacks

articles.author: Shrai Popat
articles.description:
Frontrunner Sununu beats Scott Brown to earn Republican nod in closely watched race in November
Former senator John E Sununu triumphed on Tuesday in the New Hampshire Republican Senate primary Scott Brown, earning the GOP nod in what will likely be a must-win race if Democrats hope to seize the upper chamber.
Sununu, 61, was the clear frontrunner in the GOP primary. He served one term in the Senate from 2003 to 2009.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump-backed John Sununu wins New Hampshire Republican Senate primary

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
The affluent city-state has justified high-end salaries for its political leaders, arguing they attract talent and ensure good governance
Singapore’s prime minister has been given a $1m pay rise as the affluent city-state announced a dramatic one-off salary boost for government ministers.
The pay increases add more than 60% to what are already the world’s highest ministerial salaries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Singapore boosts PM’s salary by $1m amid major pay rise for ministers

articles.author: Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
A total of six people apprehended as clean-up of rubbish stacked 10 metres high cost about £6m
Two men have been arrested after fly-tippers dumped a “mountain of illegal waste”, stacked 10 metres high, in Oxfordshire.
Hundreds of tonnes of rubbish appeared in a field between the River Cherwell and the A34 near Kidlington in November last year. The waste tip was so large that removing it could cost more than the local council’s annual budget, the area’s MP said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two more people arrested over ‘mountain of illegal waste’ dumped in Oxfordshire

articles.author: ​Vikram Dodd, Ben Quinn, Rajeev Syal
articles.description:
Whitehall officials ask why laws meant to clamp down on mask wearing at demonstrations were not used
Police have been told by the government they expect better intelligence gathering after masked far-right groups took to the streets at the weekend, the Guardian has learned, as the Kent force admitted mishandling warnings of potential trouble.
Police in Kent on Saturday and then Portsmouth, Hampshire, on Sunday said they were taken by surprise when hundreds massed to oppose what they say is illegal immigration via small boats.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Far-right port protests: police told to improve intelligence gathering

articles.author: Charlie Moloney (now) and Andrew Sparrow (earlier)
articles.description:
Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Saar, earlier claimed that the UK was ‘systemically working against the state of Israel’ 

UK accuses Israeli ‘terrorists’ of ethnic cleansing in West Bank with government backing

The Liberal Democrats say they have been granted a Commons urgent question today about the latest Argentinian threats to the Falkland Islands. A Foreign Office minister will be responding at about 12.30pm.
Isaac Herzog, the Israeli president, has said that Britain will be “on the wrong side of history” if it goes ahead with plans to ban trade with the illegal settlements on the West Bank.
Later today, we expect to see headlines announcing certain British trade sanctions on Israeli settlements in Judea and Samaria.
If this happens – and other nations may join – I believe it will prove to be a grave miscalculation, a decision that will fall on the wrong side of history.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham says Britain will ‘continue to act in support of our values’ after UK launches sanctions on Israel – as it happened

articles.author: Pippa Crerar, Jessica Elgot and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
Ed Miliband announces sanctions on trade with settlements as PM says in the Guardian it is time to act

I believe in a two-state solution in the Middle East. That’s why we’re taking action to keep that hope alive | Andy Burnham

Settler terrorists supported by Benjamin Netanyahu’s government are committing ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, Ed Miliband has said, in the UK’s starkest condemnation since the foundation of the Israeli state.
Andy Burnham, the prime minister, said he would “not stand by” as horrific suffering continued, writing in the Guardian that for too long the UK had been hesitant to act, “fearful of being accused of being anti-Israel”.
An import ban on goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories and a new ban for arms licences and other exports that “materially contribute to the occupation”.
A comprehensive sanctions regime against providing services such as construction or financing for Israeli settlements and a ban on advertising them in the UK.
Personal sanctions against key individuals accused of promoting settler violence.
A new ban for arms licences and other exports that “materially contribute to the occupation”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK accuses Israeli ‘terrorists’ of ethnic cleansing in West Bank with government backing

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Foreign secretary ends UK’s feigned helplessness with sanctions and condemnation of ‘ethnic cleansing’

Will UK sanctions have any impact on ‘settler terrorists’? 

The indefatigable ability of UK Foreign Office ministers over decades to issue boilerplate statements of concern about the extension of illegal settlements in Israel has long been a matter of ridicule.
Even some of the Conservative ministers who issued them, notably Alan Duncan and Alistair Burt, have agreed. Duncan described the UK stance towards settlements as weak and naive, while Burt wondered at the ability of the Foreign Office to find new forms of diplomatic condemnation that never amounted to any specific action. Margaret Thatcher, often torn as prime minister between her natural sympathy for Israel and her fear of the Gulf states falling under the sway of the Soviet Union, similarly expressed her anger at the settlements.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ed Miliband has overturned decades of Foreign Office inertia on illegal Israeli settlements

articles.author: Dan Milmo and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
Lisa Nandy says government will introduce legislation after talks end without breakthrough
Apple and Google will be forced to block explicit images on children’s smartphones by law in the UK after talks failed to produce a breakthrough, the government has said.
The legislation commitment puts ministers on a collision course with two of the biggest players in Silicon Valley, months after the government announced a social media ban for under-16s.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to force Apple and Google to block explicit images on children’s smartphones

articles.author: Luke Harding in London and Amy Hawkins in Kharkiv
articles.description:
Ruslan Kravchenko resigns over allegations some of his officials were engaged in large-scale money laundering
Ukraine’s prosecutor general has resigned after investigators used ladders to raid his office in connection with a major corruption scandal that threatens to embarrass Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Ruslan Kravchenko quit his post on Monday after allegations that some of his officials were involved in large-scale money laundering. They received cash to protect call centres involved in illegal phone scams, it was claimed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukraine’s prosecutor general quits after anti-corruption agents raid his office

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh and Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Comments in virtual meeting aimed at securing 300 Patriot missiles for Kyiv come as UK commits £100m for Ukraine’s air defences 
The US undersecretary of defence, Elbridge Colby, told European countries they “must not slacken” in their remilitarisation and their backing for Ukraine in a virtual meeting aimed at securing 300 Patriot interceptors for Kyiv.
The influential Pentagon official praised Ukraine’s recent “stout defence”, which he said proved that Europe was capable of leading the defence of its own continent from Russian aggression rather than relying on the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Remilitarisation and support for Ukraine must not slacken, US tells Europe

articles.author: Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent
articles.description:
Several MPs also banned from Israel after UK steps up condemnation of settlements and announces sweeping sanctions
Israel has ordered the closure of the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem in response to sweeping UK sanctions on goods from illegal settlements.
Reacting to Ed Miliband’s description of violent Jewish settler activity on the occupied Palestinian West Bank as “ethnic cleansing” carried out with the tacit backing of the Netanyahu government, Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, announced retaliatory measures including the closure of the consulate and entry bans on several UK MPs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israel to close British consulate in Jerusalem after sanctions announced

articles.author: Jakub Krupa and Yohannes Lowe
articles.description:
Moscow’s foreign minister issues warning to ‘Russophobic lobby in Budapest’ after diplomats expelled for ‘unacceptable’ activities
But the tone coming from Moscow is very different, as Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told reporters that Russia was very confident that victory in its war against Ukraine is “very near.”
“Yes, we are ​confident, and we ⁠are ​sure that ​victory ​is very near,” ​Peskov ‌said in comments reported by Reuters.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russia says it will give a ‘harsh and painful’ response after Hungary expels 10 diplomats - Europe live

articles.author: Geneva Abdul
articles.description:
Mira Lozi says quiet diplomacy has failed to free Rami Naimi who was first seized in Dubai in 2017
A British woman has spoken out for the first time about the alleged abduction, torture and coercion of her husband at the hands of Saudi authorities, after nine years of “failed” quiet diplomacy.
The businessman Rami Naimi was first abducted in Dubai in 2017 on his return from a trip to Australia with his father. After being tortured, he was released the following year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British family of man abducted by Saudi Arabia speak out over nine-year ordeal

articles.author: Jon Henley and Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
Thieves took four artworks but it is thought they dropped two in museum garden as they fled
French police are hunting two thieves who escaped with two Renoir paintings from a museum on the French Riviera after breaking in through a hole cut in its garden fence.
Bryan Masson, the mayor of Cagnes-sur-Mer, about 10 miles west of Nice, said the pair appeared to have been “well equipped and well informed” about the museum, which houses works by the French impressionist Pierre-Auguste Renoir in his former home.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Artworks stolen from Renoir Museum on French Riviera in latest heist

articles.author: Tory Shepherd
articles.description:
New research shows turbulent flushes create toilet-generated aerosols that can transmit legionella, influenza and norovirus
Flushing toilets release particles into the “breathing zone” of adults and can remain suspended in the air for at least 20 seconds, a new study has found.
And closing the lid might not be enough to avoid a “plume” of potential pathogens.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flushing the toilet can release a ‘plume’ of breathable pathogens – and closing the lid won’t stop their escape

articles.author: Andrew Messenger
articles.description:
Pre-inquest conference into Queensland deaths hears witnesses did not hear any smoke alarms during 2023 fire

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A landlord was repeatedly warned about improperly installed smoke alarms before a house fire that killed a father and five children in Queensland in 2023, a coroner has heard.
Deputy state coroner Donald MacKenzie held a pre-inquest conference into the Russell Island deaths on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mother flagged faulty smoke alarms before house fire that killed father and five children, court hears

articles.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
articles.description:
Shinjuku ward targets accommodation in residential areas and near cultural sites as locals complain visitors disposing of rubbish improperly and being too noisy
A neighbourhood in Tokyo popular with foreign tourists will ban visitors from using thousands of short-term rental accommodations after a slew of complaints about behaviour.
In the latest sign that Japan’s patience with mass tourism is wearing thin, Shinjuku ward – home to the notorious Kabukicho nightlife district and the world’s busiest railway station – will prevent visitors from using private lodgings in residential areas and near schools and important cultural sites, Japanese media reported this week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tokyo tourist hotspot bans short-term rentals amid surge in complaints

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
India’s statistical system once commanded respect, and its data on economic and social indicators was considered rigorous – that appears to have eroded
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
There isn’t much that we Indians agree on these days. GDP numbers are no exception. Last week, India released glowing GDP numbers for the latest quarter – 7.8% growth – higher than the forecast 7%. It sparked a furore.
Subhash Garg, a former finance secretary under Narendra Modi’s government and now a critic, reframed what Modi called a “herculean feat” as mere smoke and mirrors. According to Garg, the government revised last year’s current-price GDP downwards to inflate this year’s number – he believes the real growth is only 2.6%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Trust deficit’: Why India’s economic data has sparked a furore

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
Counter-measures covering several sectors come after Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian goods 
Canada’s retaliatory tariffs on billions of dollars’ worth of American imports have come into effect, escalating a trade fight that has been marked by intensifying tensions between the US president, Donald Trump, and the Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney.
The tariffs took effect at 12.01am on Tuesday, and range from 15% to 50% and apply to products covering $20bn in imports from the US. The measures target sectors including steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics – industries that have been most affected by US tariffs.
Agence France-Presse and Reuters contributed reporting
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada’s retaliatory US tariffs take effect as trade dispute grows

articles.author: Mohamed Gabobe in Mogadishu and Peter Beaumont
articles.description:
US-Israel war on Iran and political instability in Somalia lead to pirates targeting cargo ships off Horn of Africa
The scourge of Somali piracy targeting cargo ships and smaller dhows off the Horn of Africa has returned to levels not seen in a decade, driven by a convergence of factors including disruptions to the shipping industry caused by the US-Israeli war against Iran and a resurgence of political instability in Somalia.
Since late April there have been eight hijackings by Somali pirates, including two within the space of a fortnight in August: one targeting an oil tanker with ties to Iran, the other a Cameroon-flagged vessel, the Lutuf, carrying military equipment for Turkey.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hijacking pirates exploit regional chaos to return to seas off Somalia

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Ensenada
articles.description:
Bereaved mother Debra Robinson in court stares at three men accused of murdering Jake and Callum Robinson and Jack Carter Rhoad in 2024
The suspected murderers of two Australian surfers and an American at a Mexican surfing hotspot have gone on trial, two years after the killings in a suspected robbery.
Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33 respectively, and their 30-year-old American friend Jack Carter Rhoad were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast when they were shot dead in Baja California state.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I heard a lot of noise’: trial begins in Mexico for alleged killers of Australian surfers and American friend

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Kathmandu
articles.description:
Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions 
Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.
Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster

articles.author: Pjotr Sauer
articles.description:
Connection across Tumen River is further sign of closer ties between the two countries since start of war in Ukraine

Russia and North Korea have opened the first road bridge across their shared border, in the latest sign of the rapidly deepening ties between the two countries since the start of the war in Ukraine.
The one-kilometre bridge spans the Tumen River between Khasan in Russia’s far east and Tumangang in North Korea, along a remote and sparsely populated stretch of the countries’ shared border just a few miles from the coast.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russia and North Korea open first road bridge across their shared border

articles.author: Alice Nightingale-Smith for MetDesk
articles.description:
Torrential rain causes widespread damage; while north-west South Africa hit by thunderstorms and central-southern US faces oppressive heat
Typhoon Saudel brought days of torrential rain to Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian and Guangdong provinces in south-east China last week. The city of Putian, in Fujian province, recorded 416.5mm of rain in a 24-hour period between Thursday and Friday, with surrounding villages recording more than 500mm in the same period. In Fujian, authorities estimate that almost 600,000 people were evacuated from high-risk, flood-prone areas. A further 128,000 people in 53 counties were also affected across Jiangxi, with emergency evacuations affecting 9,000 people.
Flooding, landslips and infrastructure damage were reported widely in the region. More than 2,500 teachers and students were trapped in a school compound in the Zhejiang city of Wenzhou on Wednesday after extreme rainfall caused flash floods in low-lying areas. At least 1,260 people reportedly had to be rescued in Putian after a river embankment collapsed on Thursday, flattening 100 homes. On Saturday, a landslip in a village of Suichuan county, in Jiangxi province, killed three people and nine others remaining missing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Weather tracker: Typhoon Saudel causes mass evacuations in south-east China

articles.author: Ben Doherty, Andy Ball and Nick Evershed
articles.description:
Exclusive: US-controlled weapons corporations and forces have control or access to more than 100 facilities across the continent, which some analysts describe as a ‘colonisation’ of Australia’s military. Find a map of them here

US military presence in Australia, mapped – video

Why can the US access so many Australian military bases? – podcast

US military interests control or have access to more than 100 defence facilities on Australian soil, in what some analysts describe as a “saturation” – even a “colonisation” – of the Australian continent.
New data compiled by the Nautilus Institute and published by Guardian Australia maps the extent of US militarisation. The US military controls 17 facilities on mainland Australia and has access to 75 more Australian-run military installations. US defence corporations have access to an additional 18.
Gathering intelligence, accessing satellite data for targeting information and communications intercepts.
Training, including for 2,500 marines on dry-season rotation in the Northern Territory.
Pre-positioning warfighting assets such as Osprey aircraft.
Logistics hubs holding weapons, munitions and fuel, stored in case of a war in the Pacific.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The US now has access to more than half Australia’s military bases – could it drag the country unwillingly into war?

articles.author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
articles.description:
Slavery’s legacy continues ‘to deprive our country and our people’, says minister, as group prepares to appeal to Jamaica’s head of state
A landmark petition is to be handed to King Charles by Jamaica over slavery reparations, aiming to confront historical crimes that still disadvantage former British colonies, the Caribbean nation’s culture minister has said.
The petition will be lodged with Charles, Jamaica’s head of state, on Monday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jamaican delegates arrive in UK to hand slavery reparations petition to King Charles

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Beijing wants banks and insurers to bolster investment in stock market as it helps to replenish cash reserves
China will inject $54bn (£40bn) into its financial sector as Beijing attempts to shore up banks and insurers in the face of faltering economic growth.
A host of financial institutions said they were due to receive billions of yuan in capital from state institutions including the ministry of finance and even the company that runs the country’s tobacco monopoly.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: China prepares £40bn stimulus for financial sector amid fears over sluggish growth

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Tan Dhesi says Argentinian threats make it more crucial than ever that PM increase defence spending
Javier Milei’s threats to the Falkland Islands make it even more important that Andy Burnham increase defence spending immediately, according to the Labour chair of the defence committee.
Tan Dhesi said the comments by the Argentinian president this week show why the government should raise military spending to 3% of GDP by 2030. But he said Burnham’s plans remain mired in confusion after the prime minister appeared to reassure him that the 2030 target would be hit, only for Downing Street to later retreat.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Falklands row shows urgent need to commit to 3% target, says Labour defence committee chair

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
US president suggests he might support his Argentinian ally’s drive to reclaim sovereignty of disputed islands
Donald Trump has long embraced vengeance. “I am your retribution,” he declared to an admiring audience at the 2023 Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) as he commenced his march back to the White House.
It is unlikely Argentina, and far-flung holdovers of the former British empire, were on the US president’s mind at the time.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s pique with UK could lead to favor to acolyte Milei over Falklands

articles.author: AFP in Cairo
articles.description:
Sarah Khalifa, 39, charged with forming organised criminal gang to manufacture and traffic drugs
An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drug case, official media reported on Saturday.
The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her programme Mission Impossible, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Egyptian TV presenter among 12 sentenced to death for drug crime

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
articles.description:
Togo-sponsored resolution called to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland
The United Nations has voted to adopt a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size.
In a session at its headquarters in New York, the UN general assembly officially retired the 16th-century Mercator projection in favour of one based on the more accurate 2018 Equal Earth design.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UN votes to adopt new world map that shows Africa’s true scale

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu
articles.description:
Officials say pair were rescued from Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel in Nepal after being trapped at depth of 170 metres
Two people have been pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal nine days after deadly flash floods buried the projects in deep mud and left them trapped.
The workers were rescued during an operation at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, a hydropower project in one of the areas worst affected by last week’s floods, according to the army spokesperson Brig Gen Raja Ram Basnet.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two workers pulled alive from tunnel nine days after Nepal-Tibet floods

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu
articles.description:
About 46 people believed to be trapped in ‘room-like’ structure inside hydro plant tunnel on Nepal-Tibet border

After the flood: human suffering on an unfathomable scale in Nepal’s worst-hit districts

Nepal authorities have said they are “confident” that dozens of workers in Nepal’s Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant are still alive, more than a week after deadly flash floods left them trapped in an underground chamber.
Authorities said that at least 639 workers were still missing from hydropower plants built along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Triushuli rivers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Dozens of trapped hydropower tunnel workers in Nepal could still be alive, official says

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Bangladeshi complainants allege Rampal power station’s pollution and climate risks threaten the Sunderbans, a world heritage site
Barclays Bank is facing a formal complaint over its financial links to a coal-fired power station near the Sundarbans, the world’s largest mangrove forest and home to millions of people in Bangladesh and India.
Three complainants from the region have submitted a case to the UK government’s Office for Responsible Business Conduct, alleging that the British bank breached international guidelines by underwriting companies involved in the emission-heavy Maitree super thermal power project, also known as the Rampal power plant.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Barclays faces complaint over backing for power plant near world’s largest mangrove forest

articles.author: Dani Anguiano, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Missouri congressional maps thrown into chaos after conflicting court rulings

Sign up for US Breaking News emails

Further down the ballot in New Hampshire, the Democratic primary for Chris Pappas’s House seat has drawn eight candidates, with Stefany Shaheen – daughter of the outgoing senator – and Maura Sullivan, a former Obama administration official, leading the field.
The district, long purple, has been reliably blue since 2017. Republicans now see it as flippable, and Donald Trump has endorsed Anthony DiLorenzo, a businessman who owns several car dealerships, in the GOP race.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US supreme court rejects Missouri Republicans’ appeal to use Trump-backed congressional map in midterms – as it happened

articles.author: Shrai Popat in Washington
articles.description:
Tit-for-tat violence surges again in region, with tankers struck by the US in the Gulf of Oman, and reprisal attacks by Iran on a US base in Jordan
The US military on Tuesday said it “destroyed” multiple Iranian tankers, after Iran attempted to strike a US navy warship with ballistic missiles, as violence once again surged across the region, pushing the price of oil close to $100 a barrel.
American forces struck the tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Iran’s Kharg Island, US central command (Centcom) said in a statement, adding that American forces “directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US says Iranian tankers ‘destroyed’ after missile attacks on American warship

articles.author: Shrai Popat
articles.description:
Frontrunner Sununu beats Scott Brown to earn Republican nod in closely watched race in November
Former senator John E Sununu triumphed on Tuesday in the New Hampshire Republican Senate primary Scott Brown, earning the GOP nod in what will likely be a must-win race if Democrats hope to seize the upper chamber.
Sununu, 61, was the clear frontrunner in the GOP primary. He served one term in the Senate from 2003 to 2009.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump-backed John Sununu wins New Hampshire Republican Senate primary

articles.author: Shrai Popat
articles.description:
Pappas fends off challenge from progressive Karishma Manzur in seat to be vacated by retiring Jeanne Shaheen
Congressman Chris Pappas beat back progressive challenger Karishma Manzur in the Democratic primary for US Senate on Tuesday, advancing as most observers expected to what will be a closely watched general election that is critical to Democratic hopes of flipping the upper chamber.
The two were competing for the nomination that opened up after Jeanne Shaheen, 79, the state’s three‑term incumbent Democratic senator, announced her retirement.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Congressman Chris Pappas wins New Hampshire Democratic Senate primary

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The measure comes as Canada imposes $20bn in retaliatory tariffs and Canadian prime minister Mark Carney vows to reduce his country’s economic dependence on the US
The US is banning dairy products, most alcoholic beverages and motorcycles from Canada, the White House said Tuesday, as the trade war between the two neighbors and longtime allies escalates.
The ban will take effect in three weeks and comes after Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on $20bn in US imports earlier Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US bans Canadian dairy, alcohol and motorcycles as trade war with longtime ally escalates

articles.author: Margaret Sullivan
articles.description:
The more defense secretary Pete Hegseth tries to flex his manly strength, the wimpier he looks
The more the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, tries to flex his manly strength, the wimpier he looks.
The former Fox News host has attempted to seize control of what the public is allowed to know, but bad news keeps creeping out from the Pentagon.
Margaret Sullivan is a Guardian US columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mass polygraphs at the Pentagon show Hegseth’s weakness | Margaret Sullivan

articles.author: Ezra Levin and Leah Greenberg
articles.description:
Candidates must focus on two issues: affordability and accountability. They are not competing priorities
As the November election approaches with control of the House and Senate on the line, the stakes are high. With so much riding on the outcome, there is no shortage of debate about the message Democrats need to win.
Affordability has emerged as a shared – if often undefined – rallying cry. Working families are struggling with rising costs and looking for answers. But too often, we’ve seen affordability positioned as the beginning and end of the plan. Meanwhile, many see holding the Trump administration accountable for its corruption and harms as at odds with a relentless focus on kitchen-table issues.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrats need to win. Here’s the message our research says works

articles.author: Marina Villeneuve in Lynchburg, Virginia
articles.description:
Many four-year colleges will resort to laying off faculty, cutting services and increasing prices amid financial stress
Nalia Mutz started her freshman year at the University of Lynchburg in 2022 knowing exactly where she wanted to be four years later: right on track toward her dream of becoming a doctor.
When the university eliminated a dozen majors in 2024, the resulting layoffs left fewer professors to teach the science courses she needed to graduate. She began to fear earning her biomedicine degree the way she had planned could take two extra years.
Roughly 1,100 out of the 1,900 colleges in our dataset experienced enrollment drops in three of the five years from 2019 to 2024, the most recent year for which data is available. About 6.4 million students attended these schools.
About 1,500 colleges saw net revenue from tuition drop from 2019 to 2024.
Roughly 960 institutions, enrolling 5.2 million students, had 75,600 fewer instructional staff in that period.
Nearly 440 colleges and universities reported ending the financial year in the red in three of those five years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Students are suffering from US colleges’ shaky finances. Trump policies are making everything worse

articles.author: Robert Reich
articles.description:
The president apparently plans to focus on the person he most admires – himself – even if Republicans would rather he didn’t
With the midterm races officially beginning this week, a big question hanging over the Republican party is how Trump will allocate his giant stash of Super Pac money. As of 31 July, Maga Inc had more than $400m on hand, larger than the cash reserves of any of the major party committees.
But he’s barely spent any of it yet. Why not?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donald Trump’s midterm strategy? Make it all about him | Robert Reich

articles.author: Steven Greenhouse
articles.description:
Labor experts stunned at how anti-worker Trump has been with actions since last Labor Day that have hurt unions
Donald Trump has repeatedly vowed to champion US workers. Shortly before Labor Day last year, he said: “Every policy of the Trump administration is designed to lift up the American worker and “promote great-paying blue-collar jobs”. But in the year since last Labor Day, Trump has taken many actions that have hurt US workers and unions, with some labor experts saying they have been stunned at how anti-worker Trump has been.
In the months after Trump returned to office, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (Osha) cut workplace inspections by 20%, compared with Joe Biden’s last year in office. Even though Trump campaigned as a champion of coalminers, his administration has repeatedly delayed implementation of a rule to limit silica dust, which has afflicted and killed many coalminers with black lung. The United Mine Workers union has urgently called for “immediate enforcement” of the stalled silica dust rule.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The most anti-union president’: how Trump turned his back on US workers

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
A historically unpopular president will take centre stage as the party seeks to sway voters with an unprecedented event
It seemed like a good idea at the time. In December 1978, Jimmy Carter, a US president besieged by inflation and energy crises, watched as thousands of Democrats descended on Memphis, Tennessee, for a rare midterm convention.
“It was wild,” recalls Elaine Kamarck, who attended as a 28-year-old working for the Democratic National Committee. “It became a forum for Ted Kennedy to informally announce his opposition to President Carter. There was a lot of hostility to the president there. The Democrats have sworn ever since never to do anything this stupid again.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican midterm convention will be ‘Trumpist pageantry’ – at the party’s own risk

articles.author: Lok Darjee
articles.description:
Montana’s Sam Forstag says US working class is left playing a game of chance while neither party serves its interests
At around five o’clock on a winter evening in 2013, then college student Sam Forstag was driving through a snowstorm toward his third job of the day, making sandwiches at the Subway inside a Walmart.
“I was always late,” Forstag recalled with a laugh more than a decade later.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: This smokejumper says the US has lost its empathy. That’s why he’s running for Congress

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Todd Blanche’s remarks are part of a totally-not-invented moral panic that stretches the limits of the imagination
Being a public school teacher in the US these days is tough. You’ve got to pay for a lot of your own supplies, deal with smartphone-addicted children and perform gender-affirming surgeries on your lunch break.
Luckily our intrepid attorney general, Todd Blanche, is on the case. Blanche appeared on Fox News this week to decry a “pandemic” of gender transitions in schools across the US. “There’s not a parent in America, no matter where you live, that would want their school to change and call their child by a different name and not expect to be told about that. We partnered with the Department of Education recently to combat this very trend and, really, pandemic that’s happening in some school districts around the country,” Blanche said. He seemed more concerned with name changes than with surgery, but the president himself has suggested on several occasions that schools are furtively doing surgery on children. During a campaign speech in 2024, for example, Donald Trump said: “Can you imagine … your son leaves the house and you say: ‘Jimmy, I love you so much. Go have a good day in school,’ and your son comes back with a brutal operation? Can you even imagine this?”
Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The US attorney general is fretting about a ‘pandemic’ of gender transitions in schools | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.description:
The Canadian province's premier, Doug Ford, installed a billboard-sized sign on the lake's shoreline after the US president signed an executive order on Thursday directing US federal agencies to change the lake's name on US maps, documents and databases to 'Lake America'. Ford told reporters that the lake's name, which is more than 400 years old, would remain unchanged. Trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed last week, with each side ‌blaming the ⁠other for derailing three days of intensive negotiations


Trump signs executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ontario premier unveils Lake Ontario sign in response to Trump’s ‘Lake America’ order – video

articles.description:
Jonathan Freedland speaks to Dan Alexander of Forbes about how Donald Trump made so much money last year at the same time trade wars, military wars and a rising national debt hurt the US economy
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How did Trump get so rich? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Paul Owen ; produced by Bryony Moore ; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
One of Donald Trump’s closest and most devoted aides, Natalie Harp, has faced intense media scrutiny this week, after a Democratic senator, Jon Ossoff, name-checked her in a speech that went viral. So what do we know about Harp, who is often referred to as the ‘human printer’? And why is everybody talking about her relationship with Trump? Helen Pidd speaks to international news editor Paul Owen
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why is Trump’s ‘human printer’ aide Natalie Harp suddenly in the spotlight? - The Latest

articles.author: Jonathan Freedland with Jill Lepore . Produced by Nada Smiljanic, and Danielle Stephens
articles.description:
Less than three months to go until the midterms, voters are thinking about grocery prices, the Iran war and… datacentres.

This week, Jonathan Freedland speaks to historian Jill Lepore about how this latest AI backlash could influence those all-important elections in November. Are we seeing the beginning of the end of the 'artificial state'?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Historian Jill Lepore on the datacentre backlash | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
More than 1,000 flights cancelled with disruption continuing on Wednesday and airlines calling for overhaul after third incident in just over three years

UK airport disruption: what are your rights?

Flight delays and cancellations were expected to continue into Wednesday at UK airports after another air traffic control failure kept planes grounded for hours, affecting hundreds of thousands of passengers.
At least 177 flights scheduled for Wednesday to and from UK airports had been cancelled, plane tracking site Flightradar24 said, “nearly all at London Heathrow”. More than 1,000 were cancelled by about 8pm on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK air traffic control breakdown strands hundreds of thousands of passengers

articles.author: Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
A total of six people apprehended as clean-up of rubbish stacked 10 metres high cost about £6m
Two men have been arrested after fly-tippers dumped a “mountain of illegal waste”, stacked 10 metres high, in Oxfordshire.
Hundreds of tonnes of rubbish appeared in a field between the River Cherwell and the A34 near Kidlington in November last year. The waste tip was so large that removing it could cost more than the local council’s annual budget, the area’s MP said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two more people arrested over ‘mountain of illegal waste’ dumped in Oxfordshire

articles.author: ​Vikram Dodd, Ben Quinn, Rajeev Syal
articles.description:
Whitehall officials ask why laws meant to clamp down on mask wearing at demonstrations were not used
Police have been told by the government they expect better intelligence gathering after masked far-right groups took to the streets at the weekend, the Guardian has learned, as the Kent force admitted mishandling warnings of potential trouble.
Police in Kent on Saturday and then Portsmouth, Hampshire, on Sunday said they were taken by surprise when hundreds massed to oppose what they say is illegal immigration via small boats.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Far-right port protests: police told to improve intelligence gathering

articles.author: Charlie Moloney (now) and Andrew Sparrow (earlier)
articles.description:
Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Saar, earlier claimed that the UK was ‘systemically working against the state of Israel’ 

UK accuses Israeli ‘terrorists’ of ethnic cleansing in West Bank with government backing

The Liberal Democrats say they have been granted a Commons urgent question today about the latest Argentinian threats to the Falkland Islands. A Foreign Office minister will be responding at about 12.30pm.
Isaac Herzog, the Israeli president, has said that Britain will be “on the wrong side of history” if it goes ahead with plans to ban trade with the illegal settlements on the West Bank.
Later today, we expect to see headlines announcing certain British trade sanctions on Israeli settlements in Judea and Samaria.
If this happens – and other nations may join – I believe it will prove to be a grave miscalculation, a decision that will fall on the wrong side of history.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham says Britain will ‘continue to act in support of our values’ after UK launches sanctions on Israel – as it happened

articles.author: Pippa Crerar, Jessica Elgot and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
Ed Miliband announces sanctions on trade with settlements as PM says in the Guardian it is time to act

I believe in a two-state solution in the Middle East. That’s why we’re taking action to keep that hope alive | Andy Burnham

Settler terrorists supported by Benjamin Netanyahu’s government are committing ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, Ed Miliband has said, in the UK’s starkest condemnation since the foundation of the Israeli state.
Andy Burnham, the prime minister, said he would “not stand by” as horrific suffering continued, writing in the Guardian that for too long the UK had been hesitant to act, “fearful of being accused of being anti-Israel”.
An import ban on goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories and a new ban for arms licences and other exports that “materially contribute to the occupation”.
A comprehensive sanctions regime against providing services such as construction or financing for Israeli settlements and a ban on advertising them in the UK.
Personal sanctions against key individuals accused of promoting settler violence.
A new ban for arms licences and other exports that “materially contribute to the occupation”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK accuses Israeli ‘terrorists’ of ethnic cleansing in West Bank with government backing

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Foreign secretary ends UK’s feigned helplessness with sanctions and condemnation of ‘ethnic cleansing’

Will UK sanctions have any impact on ‘settler terrorists’? 

The indefatigable ability of UK Foreign Office ministers over decades to issue boilerplate statements of concern about the extension of illegal settlements in Israel has long been a matter of ridicule.
Even some of the Conservative ministers who issued them, notably Alan Duncan and Alistair Burt, have agreed. Duncan described the UK stance towards settlements as weak and naive, while Burt wondered at the ability of the Foreign Office to find new forms of diplomatic condemnation that never amounted to any specific action. Margaret Thatcher, often torn as prime minister between her natural sympathy for Israel and her fear of the Gulf states falling under the sway of the Soviet Union, similarly expressed her anger at the settlements.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ed Miliband has overturned decades of Foreign Office inertia on illegal Israeli settlements

articles.author: Dan Milmo and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
Lisa Nandy says government will introduce legislation after talks end without breakthrough
Apple and Google will be forced to block explicit images on children’s smartphones by law in the UK after talks failed to produce a breakthrough, the government has said.
The legislation commitment puts ministers on a collision course with two of the biggest players in Silicon Valley, months after the government announced a social media ban for under-16s.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to force Apple and Google to block explicit images on children’s smartphones

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
articles.description:
A look at whether Ed Miliband’s plans will be effective and what they signal for future Israel-UK relations

UK politics live – latest updates

The British foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has announced plans for an import ban on goods from illegal settlements in occupied Palestine and sanctions for companies that “finance or facilitate” the construction, infrastructure and marketing of illegal settlements.
He also said “settler terrorists” were perpetrating ethnic cleansing in the occupied West Bank, while the government turned a blind eye and some members supported it.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Will UK sanctions have any impact on Israel’s ‘settler terrorists’ in West Bank?

articles.author: Siraj Datoo (now), Charlie Moloney and Graeme Wearden (earlier)
articles.description:
National Air Traffic Services apologise for technical issue disrupting departures today, which Flightradar24 say has caused hundreds of cancellations

Air traffic control issue causes flight delays and disruption across UK

Gas prices are rising this morning, putting pressure on European countries who need to stock up their storage levels before the winter.
The month-ahead UK gas price is up around 1% at 184p a therm, close to yesterday’s highs when gas hit its highest since January 2023.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More than 600 UK flights cancelled after air traffic control ‘technical issue’ – as it happened

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Seaside communities and businesses were affected significantly by the contamination in June 2023
United Utilities has been fined nearly £1m after illegally discharging raw sewage along the Lancashire coastline and polluting seaside holiday locations including Blackpool.
The water company pleaded guilty to five environmental permit offences relating to a pollution incident along the Fylde coast in June 2023, and was ordered by Preston magistrates court on Tuesday to pay £964,225 in fines and costs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: United Utilities fined nearly £1m after discharging raw sewage along Lancashire coast

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
articles.description:
Tickets set to cost £408 at return for Somerset festival after a fallow year, a jump from £378.50 in 2025
After a fallow year in 2026, Glastonbury festival fans can start to get excited – and nervous – about tickets for 2027’s event going on sale.
The price breaks £400 for the first time, at £408 including a £5 booking fee, a rise from the 2025 cost of £378.50. The usual scramble to acquire them – with all the attendant frantic spreadsheets and WhatsApp groups – will begin at 9am on Sunday 4 October.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Glastonbury tickets break £400 for first time as on-sale date is announced

articles.author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
articles.description:
High yields threaten to wipe out at least half of the £24bn headroom John Healey was expecting to have for his budget
The UK government was forced to pay the highest interest rate for a 30-year bond since 1998 on Tuesday, underlining the fiscal challenges facing the chancellor, John Healey.
Echoing the global bond market sell-off that has driven up yields, or interest rates, on government borrowing across the main markets, the Treasury paid 5.82% to borrow £4bn.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK government pays highest interest rate on 30-year bond since 1998

articles.author: Zoe Wood and Rupert Jones
articles.description:
Air traffic control issue affecting airports across UK on Tuesday has been resolved but disruption could continue into Wednesday

Flight disruption continues after air traffic control technical issue

Airports across the UK including Manchester, Birmingham and all those in London were hit by problems at air traffic control on Tuesday.
The technical issue was announced shortly before 2pm and was resolved about three hours later. By that time, hundreds of flights had been cancelled, with knock-on disruption across Britain and at destination airports abroad likely to continue into the evening and possibly Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK airport disruption: what are your rights if you have been affected?

UK accuses Israeli ‘terrorists’ of ethnic cleansing in West Bank with government backing

articles.title: UK foreign secretary announces sanctions on trade with Israeli West Bank settlements – video

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
In partnership with DWP, firms such as John Lewis and M&S plan to offer 18- to 24-year-olds placements of two to four weeks
UK retailers aim to create up to 100,000 jobs for young people not in employment, education or training (Neet) over the next three years by giving them a first step on the ladder into work.
In partnership with the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), more than 40 retailers, including Marks & Spencer, Pets at Home, Asda and the John Lewis Partnership, will offer Neets aged 18-24 placements of two to four weeks to gain “the skills and confidence needed to take their first step into work”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK retailers aim to create 100,000 jobs for young people out of work

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Exclusive: London mayor accuses council of ‘ignoring’ responses to a consultation
Sadiq Khan has criticised the “breathtaking arrogance” of Westminster council, which has kept restrictions on vertical drinking in Soho and an effective ban on new bars and pubs in the area.
The mayor of London has accused the Conservative-led council of “ignoring” the responses to a consultation into its new licensing policy. The vast majority of respondents, 81%, disagreed with the council’s “cumulative impact zone” which decrees that applications for bars and pubs in the West End of London, one of Europe’s most famous nightlife districts, will be refused unless in exceptional circumstances. Eighty-four per cent said the licensing policy would be bad for business.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Curbs on vertical drinking in Soho pubs to go ahead as Khan criticises council’s ‘breathtaking arrogance’

articles.author: Emma Howard
articles.description:
More than 140 clubs breached licences, with a third caught taking water illegally, analysis shows – but no fines issued
More than 140 golf clubs in England have breached their water extraction licences in the past five years, according to data analysis by the Guardian.
More than a third of these clubs were caught taking water illegally from the environment, either by taking more than permitted or by removing it outside the permitted period.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One in 12 golf clubs in England broke water extraction rules in past five years

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
Experts helped guide weather scenes in Pressure – a film depicting dramatic buildup to 1944’s D-day landings
Dressed in a Royal Air Force uniform and sporting a trim moustache, Andrew Scott looks slightly queasy – as well he might. Behind him is a huge map of the Channel, and in front of him is Brendan Fraser, looming with a request: “I need a forecast,” he says.
Starring in the film Pressure, based on a true story, Scott plays the meteorologist Gp Capt James Stagg – the man who must tell Gen Eisenhower – played by Fraser – whether conditions will be suitable for the D-day landings scheduled to take place on 5 June 1944. But a large storm is approaching the Normandy coast.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How meteorologists recreated weather that helped decide second world war

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Rene Haas also claims artificial intelligence could pave way for widespread use of humanoid robots within five years

Business live – latest updates

The boss of one of the UK’s biggest chip companies has claimed AI will be able to find a cure for cancer “in our lifetime”.
Rene Haas, chief executive of the chip designer Arm Holdings, said that, while modelling how a DNA marker is affected by cancer was currently “too complex” a problem for either humans or technology, computers were “going to solve it” in the future.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI will help find cure for cancer ‘within our lifetimes’, says Arm Holdings chief

articles.author: Chris Wiegand Stage editor
articles.description:
Akram Khan among those paying tribute to ‘pioneering’ choreographer of intense musicality and grace who inspired generations of dancers
Sir Richard Alston, the British choreographer and teacher who took contemporary dance into new directions with his elegant and intelligent creations, has died at the age of 77. A former artistic director of Rambert and the Place, where he made more than 50 pieces for the Richard Alston Dance Company, he was celebrated for lucid, emotionally attuned work that was often as graceful as it was rigorous.
His death was announced on Monday by the Richard Alston Foundation, which was established in 2021 to promote contemporary dance and preserve his work. “It is with deep sadness that we have to report the death of Sir Richard Alston,” said the statement. “After a period of ill-health, and despite exceptional treatment at the Royal Free Hospital in Hampstead and the support of his closest friends, he passed away peacefully at his home on 7 September. While Richard is best known for his extraordinary career and contribution to contemporary dance, we will also remember him for his wit, warmth and generosity of spirit.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Richard Alston, trailblazer and guiding light of British dance, dies aged 77

articles.author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
articles.description:
Firms warn of impact of company’s decision to to axe 4,000 jobs and call for government to support sector

Jaguar Land Rover confirms plan to cut 4,000 jobs

David Roberts is not in an optimistic mood. The chair of Coventry-based Evtec may preside over a business with 900 highly skilled employees, multiple sites and precision machinery, but the outlook for the manufacturer appears tricky. “Everything is against us,” he says.
Evtec is a “tier 1” supplier to Jaguar Land Rover, also headquartered in Coventry, which this week announced 4,000 job cuts over two years even as the chancellor, John Healey, attempted to talk up Britain’s growth prospects in his first big speech, just down the road.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Everything is against us’: Jaguar Land Rover suppliers voice fears amid carmaker’s cutbacks

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Backers seek support for second attempt to get law through House of Lords after ‘undemocratic’ rejection last year
MPs on both sides of the assisted dying debate have voiced fears about turnout affecting the vote on Friday, when the bill returns to the Commons for its second attempt to become law.
Those who back the change in the law in England and Wales have been emphasising the “undemocratic” nature of the bill’s rejection by the House of Lords after it was talked out by a handful of peers after passing the House of Commons. The bill fell despite multiple days of debate from peers because of the number of amendments tabled in the Lords.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Low turnout threatens Commons vote on assisted dying, say MPs

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Ed Miliband to reassert support for Palestinian rights and a two-state solution in move fiercely criticised by US and Israel
Ed Miliband will announce a broad reset of the UK’s relations with Israel on Tuesday, promising the government will take a more active approach in supporting the Palestinian cause.
In an intervention which has already drawn fierce criticism from the US and Israel, the foreign secretary will impose a UK ban on the trade in goods and some services from illegal Israeli settlements.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to adopt tougher stance on Israel with illegal settlements trade ban

articles.author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
articles.description:
Nearly half of respondents say spending on personal independence payments should be increased
There is little appetite for cuts to disability benefits even among Conservative and Reform voters, and proposals to reduce spending could prove politically risky, according to an authoritative national survey.
The British Social Attitudes (BSA) report found that while support for welfare spending as a whole had dipped sharply in recent years, just 7% of respondents backed cuts to disability benefits – and 49% said they should be increased.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Majority of Tory and Reform voters do not back cuts to disability benefits, survey finds

articles.author: Charlie Moloney and Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
Sarah Jones tells MPs ‘those responsible should expect to face the consequences’
Healey says Andy Burnham set out in his statement to MPs last week what he thought had gone wrong
The fundamentals of our economy [were] hollowed out through a series of past policy decisions, political power was centralised, weakening the relationships between the people, the businesses and the institutions who can make things happen beyond Whitehall. The economic enablers were privatised and outsourced, leaving accountability to a thicket of arm’s length bodies and regulators, too often without the predictability or the pace that underpins a thriving market economy. And our country was deindustrialised as the cost to make anything, to build anything here soared, and our dependence on unreliable sources grew, including in areas critical to our national security and sovereignty.
Let me be clear, I recognise that the costs of business, its energy bills, regulation, burdens, planning constraints, labour costs, have grown since Covid and I want to draw the line.
And whether it is the cost of business or the cost of living, the only way we deal with these in the long term is growth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Policing minister makes statement on ‘intimidating and thuggish’ anti-migrant protests – as it happened

articles.author: Pippa Crerar and Peter Walker
articles.description:
Despite series of scandals, members remain loyal to their leader as questions over his successor grow
Few British politicians unleash the kind of evangelical zeal among their party faithful as Nigel Farage. Despite being weighed down by weeks of scandal, last weekend’s Reform UK conference showed that – as far as the membership is concerned – the lustre has not come off their man.
So it was notable that Farage felt compelled to reassure his disciples that he wasn’t going anywhere. “I’m only here because of the failure of our political class, and I am determined to lead Reform to victory at the next general election. That is my job,” he told them during his speech.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Farage still Reform’s best hope as rivals struggle to match appeal to party faithful

articles.author: Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey, produced by Frankie Tobi, Nada Smiljanic and John Rogers, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
Alternative für Deutschland has claimed a historic win in Germany, continuing the pattern of populist far-right parties gaining power across Europe.
In the UK, balaclava-clad far-right protesters have marched on Dover, and then Portsmouth, trying to intimidate asylum seekers.
Meanwhile, Reform UK’s conference ended with a beleaguered Nigel Farage dealing with protesters and allegations following an undercover investigation into party donors. Will far-right sentiment in Europe and the UK be a boost for Farage or a burden?
You can read an explainer on the Dover and Portsmouth protests here.

Netflix has announced that production has begun on a new Inbetweeners film, with the original cast members reprising their roles.
It will be a continuation of the popular Channel 4 sitcom, which aired on E4 from 2008 to 2010, followed by two films in 2011 and 2014.

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Reports of Soho Farmhouse visit add to speculation Duke and Duchess of Sussex could be settling in the area
When the Duke and Duchess of Sussex landed back in England earlier this summer, six years after they moved to California and quit as working royals, speculation was rife about where they would call home.
Now, members of the luxury countryside retreat Soho Farmhouse have said they spotted Meghan arriving for an early morning coffee, sparking speculation that the couple were settling down in the exclusive countryside enclave of north Oxfordshire. The correspondent for the Royalist Tom Sykes said the duchess was seen arriving at the Comfy Farm lounge before 9am, where she was introduced to senior staff members by name.

articles.title: Sightings of Meghan at star-studded retreat fuel Cotswolds rumours

articles.description:
Guide price of archive documenting concerts, rehearsals, soundchecks and conversations between £1.2m and £1.6m
An archive of more than 100 hours of Oasis recordings, including concerts, rehearsals and candid conversations between Noel and Liam Gallagher, is to be auctioned for up to £1.6m despite objections from the band.
The collection was amassed by the band’s sound engineer Huw Richards, who worked with Oasis from the release of their 1994 debut album, Definitely Maybe, until 2001. It comprises 209 DAT tapes, 73 analogue cassettes and three MiniDiscs, and is being sold by Richards’s son, Owain.

articles.title: Oasis recordings up for auction despite band’s objections

articles.author: Kevin Rawlinson
articles.description:
Campaigners say anti-migrant collective, which gathers together a series of local groups, is home to a host of violent criminals
Hundreds of masked and hooded anti-migrant activists descended on an English coastal town and city over the weekend, blocking traffic in and out of the port of Dover, and gathering in Portsmouth after it emerged a boatful of people had been rescued at sea and brought ashore there.
The far-right group Patriot Platform seemingly managed to plan and carry out its operations unimpeded – despite having been clear it was building up to some form of action on social media. So what is Patriot Platform?

articles.description:
Newscaster says rare but treatable condition polycythaemia vera left her feeling like she ‘had her batteries taken out’
The BBC News presenter Maryam Moshiri has been diagnosed with a rare form of incurable blood cancer, she has revealed.
Doctors told the broadcaster last November she had polycythaemia vera (PV), which cannot be cured but is treatable. The condition, which affects about 8,000 people in the UK, is associated with an increased risk of the blood clots that can cause a stroke, heart attack or deep vein thrombosis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: BBC News presenter Maryam Moshiri reveals she has incurable blood cancer

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
US-owned dating app allegedly allowed ad firms access to private information in breach of UK law
Grindr will pay £26m to settle a lawsuit brought by thousands of users in the UK who allege that the US dating app shared highly sensitive personal information, including in some cases their HIV status, with advertising companies.
The settlement brings to an end a two-year legal battle, after the UK law firm Austen Hays filed a claim at the high court of England and Wales in April 2024 on behalf of Grindr users alleging violations of UK privacy laws during a period up to early 2020.

Labour’s new powers for customers to hold water companies to account are a “stitch-up”, campaigners have said, as utilities firms have been advising on how to implement it.
The Consumer Council for Water (CCW) is creating what the government referred to as “powerful consumer panels” so the public can question the executives of their local water company and get redress for problems they face from sewage and water companies in England and Wales.
